title: Repo Governor acceptance bar, version 1
$comment: One file per authority id, at .repo-governor/acceptance/<id>.json (ADR-017). The bar states WHAT must be true for work to stop; the repository provider measures WHETHER it is. This schema is the published contract: before it existed the shape lived only in the body of ADR-017, and a governed repository authored criteria with 'command' and 'description' keys that were never read (issue 214). Enforced by adapters/acceptance-file; conformance/acceptance.py asserts the two agree.

authority_id.$comment: Must equal the file's basename and the id the engine asks for. A bar that answers about a different authority is refused rather than silently used.

criteria.$comment: An EMPTY array is not a satisfied bar. It yields NO_CRITERIA_DECLARED, never STOP_COMPLETE (issue 58).

$examples.$comment: Written by `engine/acceptance.py <id> --template` to show the criterion shape in the file the author is about to edit. Ignored by the engine -- only 'criteria' is read. Allowed here so the scaffold this project ships validates against the contract this project publishes.

$covers_if_partial.$comment: Template scaffolding, offered unset. An author renames it to 'covers' if the bar deliberately leaves part of the item out. Ignored by the engine under this name -- which is the point: a partial bar must be declared deliberately, not inherited from a template.

criterion.$comment: A criterion is exactly (check, target). Anything else is not read.

check.$comment: Closed vocabulary (ADR-017 rule 4). Growing it requires an ADR; the natural growth path ends at an expression language nobody planned.

target.$comment: What the repository provider measures: a repo-relative path for file_exists, a shell command string for tests_pass and command_exit (adapters/git evaluate_check). Required. A criterion without it states nothing measurable.

covers.$comment: A bar that covers only part of its authority. Two issues once shipped that fact in a $comment and both read STOP_COMPLETE for the whole item, because nothing mechanical reads prose.

declared.$comment: The part this bar does check.

uncovered.$comment: The part it does NOT. Required: a bar that names what it covers but not what it omits has recorded a boast, not a limit.

split_to.$comment: Authority ids the uncovered half moved to. Absent means undischarged and completion stays blocked; an EMPTY array is deleting 'covers' with extra steps and is refused the same way.

split_note.$comment: Why the split happened. Prose here is fine because it is not load-bearing; split_to is what the engine reads.

amendment.$comment: A bar edited after the fact must say so, citably. An un-cited amendment cannot be distinguished from editing the bar to fit the work, so the adapter refuses to serve the criteria at all.

cites.$comment: Verifiable references for why the bar changed -- file paths, section numbers, issue ids. Non-empty: the adapter refuses an amendment whose cites are falsy.

effect.$comment: Closed set. 'weakened' and 'removed' are the ones a reader is looking for.

reason.$comment: What changed and why, in prose. Read by humans; the cites are what make it checkable.
